name: gorm-contextual-field-access-policies
instr:
GORM cannot currently authorize model-field access by context, operation, and purpose. Add a session-scoped policy governing SQL construction and result materialization without changing established semantics.

Installing, replacing, or clearing a policy affects only the returned DB chain. Preserve one policy and initiating statement snapshot through scopes, callbacks, cloned sessions, and nested work. Decisions include context, operation, purpose, schema, field, and statement; model and database field names resolve identically.

Apply one effective decision to conditions, writes, projections, destination assignment, and relationships. Keep mandatory internal identities only for linking and matching. Preserve defaults, timestamps, generated keys, batch shape, permitted returned values, joins, preload identity, cardinality, and value alignment. Consume complete rows but do not assign denied fields.

Reject denied conditions, explicit projections, or required association keys with FieldAccessDeniedError before execution; never broaden operations or partially replace relationships. Omit denied update assignments and redact denied returning fields under the stable snapshot. Many-to-many preload must match every child using hidden identities while withholding denied values. Association failures are atomic.

Traditional and generic G operations must produce equivalent SQL, variables, errors, affected rows, and redacted results. No policy and allow-all policies preserve existing crea
